reasons: narrow: For an arbitrary rational tolerance, \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) does not measure the binary input size: it omits numerator complexity and is not even nonnegative when \(\varepsilon>1\). The proof controls the weak-optimization accuracy by the full rational encoding length. The logarithmic description is recovered for the canonical dyadic representation \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\).
